subject: 987EF0C27231E82F60711CF5B59C8BBF
introduction: A Tablet of visitation is a prayer to be said at, or toward, the resting-place of a holy person: the Báb and Bahá’u’lláh have theirs, and Bahá’u’lláh and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá wrote many for martyrs and devoted believers. They greet the departed, recall what he or she did, and ask a blessing through that life. This guide gathers them with the instructions for approaching a shrine: purify yourself, pause at the gate, ask leave. The practice comes from Shí‘ih piety. Moses at the bush, the pilgrim psalms and Mary at the tomb are its scriptural neighbours; the unknown grave of Moses, the angels’ “why seek ye the living among the dead?” and Jesus’s words about garnished sepulchres are the Bible’s reservations.
questions: What do these prayers do: honour the dead, benefit the living, or both?
Why approach a grave with the preparations reading 7 and 8 describe?
What is the difference between honouring a martyr’s tomb and what Jesus criticized?

outside.why: A visitation prayer to be recited with a group. Seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses.
Consecrate thy heart, then visit with manifest humility. Put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.
Thou art enjoying eternal life. Think not of those who are slain in the way of Allah as dead. Nay, they are living.
Glory upon all who seek out thy resting-place. Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints.
When thou desirest to begin thy visitation. I was glad when they said unto me, let us go into the house of the Lord.
Before entering that land, purify thyself. Who shall stand in his holy place? He that hath clean hands, and a pure heart.
The law of visitation: stand at the gate of the shrine. Jacob set up the stone for a pillar, and called the name of that place Beth-el.
Pray in the small chamber, then turn. Mary stood without at the sepulchre weeping.
The angels’ question to visitors at another tomb: why seek ye the living among the dead? He is not here. What do the readings say the visitor finds at a grave?
Peace be upon thee. Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord: they rest from their labours; and their works do follow them.
A Tablet of visitation revealed for one soul. Lincoln at Gettysburg: the world can never forget what they did here.
He accepts from the visitor. Of Moses it is written: no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day. Why might a religion hide a grave, and why do the readings give graves such honour?

Seek permission at the gates, then enter. Jesus on the piety of tombs: ye build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous, and say, if we had been in the days of our fathers. What would keep visitation from being that?

shortfall: Forty-eight further readings are the texts of particular Tablets of visitation, salutations to one person after another.
